title: Explainable Decision Graphs for Trustworthy Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
content: Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are in-creasingly being considered for critical applications such as healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, and autonomous transporta-tion. These systems consist of multiple intelligent agents that can independently perceive information, reason about their environment, communicate with other agents, and execute deci-sions. Although multi-agent architectures provide flexibility and scalability, their distributed decision-making process can make the overall system difficult to understand, audit, and verify. Existing Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques such as Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) primarily fo-cus on explaining individual machine-learning predictions. They provide limited support for representing collaborative reasoning, inter-agent communication, conflicts, and collective decisions. This paper proposes an Explainable Decision Graph (EDG) framework for representing the reasoning process of autonomous multi-agent systems in a structured and interpretable form. The proposed framework models agents, observations, evi-dence, communications, intermediate decisions, conflicts, verifi-cation events, and final actions as interconnected graph com-ponents. A verification layer enables decision pathways to be examined against predefined safety and policy constraints. The resulting graph can provide different levels of explanations for end users, developers, and auditors. The paper defines an experimental methodology using multi-agent execution traces and proposes evaluation through ex-planation fidelity, completeness, decision traceability, human comprehensibility, decision accuracy, explanation consistency, and computational overhead. Empirical numerical results are intentionally reserved for the implementation and evaluation stage.
